subject: math
intro: I'm Mr. Okafor. Integer operations can be confusing, so let's plan a 7th grade lesson that uses a model students can picture.

beats.narration: The balloon metaphor gives students a picture: add hot air to go up, add sandbags to go down.
beats.text: Hot Air Balloons: Adding & Subtracting Integers

beats.narration: This standard is about adding and subtracting rational numbers, including on a number line.
The "explain why" is the hard part, and it's what the balloon model is for.
beats.text: Students will be able to add and subtract integers using a number line and explain why subtracting a negative is the same as adding a positive.

beats.narration: Temperature is a familiar context that uses a number line naturally.
beats.text: Temperature changes: "It was −3°F at dawn and rose 8 degrees. What's the temperature now?" Students solve on a vertical number line.

beats.narration: Students can picture "removing a sandbag" and connect it to subtracting a negative.
beats.text: Introduce the balloon model: hot air = +1, sandbags = −1. Model adding and removing each. Removing sandbags makes the balloon go up, so subtracting a negative means going up.

beats.narration: Counters give a second model that backs up the balloon picture.
beats.text: Partner game with two-color counters: draw expression cards, model them with counters, and record the equation. Pairs race to 10 correct cards.

beats.narration: I ask for the explanation to check understanding, not just the rule.
beats.text: Solve −4 − (−6) and explain your answer with the balloon model or counters.

outro: One strong model, used throughout. Your turn to plan.
